case_title: Neeraj Sharma v. State of Chhattisgarh
trial_court_outcome: Convicted of offences under sections 307/120B, 364A and 392/397 IPC
neutral_facts: The accused, Neeraj Sharma and Ashwani Kumar Yadav, abducted the victim, Arjit Sharma, while he was staying as a paying guest in the house of Seema Singh. The victim was taken on a motorcycle ride and during the journey, the accused attempted to strangle him with the clutch wire of the motorcycle. The victim fell unconscious and the accused believed he was dead, so they poured petrol on his body and set him on fire. The victim survived and sustained severe burn injuries, which resulted in the amputation of his right leg. The victim was later rescued and taken to the hospital. The prosecution established the abduction and attempt to murder, but failed to prove the demand of ransom necessary for the offence under section 364A IPC. The victim's injuries matched the prosecution's case, and medical reports confirmed the burn injuries. The accused were convicted under sections 307, 120B, 392, and 397 IPC, but the conviction under section 364A was set aside. The conviction under section 364 IPC was affirmed, and the accused were sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for ten years each and fined Rs.10,000 each.
